title: Word formation (FCE Part 3)
note: FCE Part 3 shape: sentence gap + capitalised root, student types the WHOLE derived word · EN-only cues (James, 2026-08-18) · all sentences original

cards.title: Word formation — the exam task
cards.body: In FCE Part 3 every line gives you a sentence with a gap and a word in CAPITALS. Change the capital word so it fits the gap — usually a different word class, sometimes a negative.
points: Read the whole sentence first — it decides the word class AND whether the meaning is negative.
Type the whole word, never just the ending.
Watch for stem changes: decide → decision, choose → choice.

cards.title: Making nouns
points: Some nouns change the stem: decide → decision, choose → choice, grow → growth.

cards.title: Adjectives — and their negatives
points: Negative prefixes: un- (unlucky), in- (informal), im- before p (impossible), ir- before r (irresponsible), il- before l (illegal), dis- (dishonest).
The sentence tells you when the meaning is negative — look for signals like but, too, nobody, without.

cards.title: People, verbs and adverbs
points: -en makes verbs: short → shorten, wide → widen.

items.en: He showed great determination in finishing the race with an injured knee.
items.gap: He showed great ____ in finishing the race with an injured knee.
items.explanation: Verb → noun with -ation: determine → determination. After 'great' you need a noun.

items.en: There has been a real improvement in her writing since January.
items.gap: There has been a real ____ in her writing since January.
items.explanation: Verb → noun with -ment: improve → improvement.

items.en: Making the final decision took the committee almost a week.
items.gap: Making the final ____ took the committee almost a week.
items.explanation: Stem change: decide → decision (not 'decidement'). 'The final ___' needs a noun.

items.en: The teacher gave a clear explanation of the new rule.
items.gap: The teacher gave a clear ____ of the new rule.
items.explanation: explain → explanation — the i of 'explain' disappears.

items.en: Money alone will not bring you happiness.
items.gap: Money alone will not bring you ____.
items.explanation: Adjective → noun with -ness; y → i: happy → happiness.

items.en: Spelling is her one real weakness in writing.
items.gap: Spelling is her one real ____ in writing.
items.explanation: Adjective → noun with -ness: weak → weakness.

items.en: She has the ability to learn languages very quickly.
items.gap: She has the ____ to learn languages very quickly.
items.explanation: Stem change: able → ability. 'The ___ to do something' needs a noun.

items.en: The band gave an unforgettable performance last night.
items.gap: The band gave an unforgettable ____ last night.
items.explanation: Verb → noun with -ance: perform → performance ('give a performance').

items.en: There is a small difference in meaning between the two words.
items.gap: There is a small ____ in meaning between the two words.
items.explanation: Verb → noun with -ence: differ → difference.

items.en: They had a long argument about money in the car.
items.gap: They had a long ____ about money in the car.
items.explanation: argue → argument — the e of 'argue' disappears.

items.en: The growth of the city has been incredibly fast since 2010.
items.gap: The ____ of the city has been incredibly fast since 2010.
items.explanation: Stem change: grow → growth. 'The ___ of the city' needs a noun.

items.en: You have a choice between the morning and evening course.
items.gap: You have a ____ between the morning and evening course.
items.explanation: Big stem change: choose → choice.

items.en: Her second novel was hugely successful and sold out in weeks.
items.gap: Her second novel was hugely ____ and sold out in weeks.
items.explanation: Noun → adjective with -ful: success → successful.

items.en: It was careless of him to leave his passport on the train.
items.gap: It was ____ of him to leave his passport on the train.
items.explanation: -less = without. The mistake shows there was no care — so careless, not careful.

items.en: Flats in the city centre are too expensive for most young people.
items.gap: Flats in the city centre are too ____ for most young people.
items.explanation: Noun → adjective with -ive: expense → expensive.

items.en: The team played brilliantly but was unlucky to lose in the final minute.
items.gap: The team played brilliantly but was ____ to lose in the final minute.
items.explanation: 'but ... to lose' — the meaning is negative, so un- + lucky.

items.en: The chairs were so uncomfortable that nobody stayed for the second talk.
items.gap: The chairs were so ____ that nobody stayed for the second talk.
items.explanation: Nobody stayed — the meaning is negative: un- + comfortable.

items.en: Our old car is slow but completely reliable.
items.gap: Our old car is slow but completely ____.
items.explanation: Verb → adjective with -able; y → i: rely → reliable.

items.en: Don't be so impatient — the results come out tomorrow.
items.gap: Don't be so ____ — the results come out tomorrow.
items.explanation: The advice is to stop wanting the results NOW → negative, and im- before p.

items.en: Prague is famous for its bridges and its old town.
items.gap: Prague is ____ for its bridges and its old town.
items.explanation: Noun → adjective with -ous: fame → famous (the e disappears).

items.en: It was dishonest of her to copy her friend's homework and say nothing.
items.gap: It was ____ of her to copy her friend's homework and say nothing.
items.explanation: Copying and hiding it is the opposite of honest → dis- + honest.

items.en: Driving that fast in heavy rain was completely irresponsible.
items.gap: Driving that fast in heavy rain was completely ____.
items.explanation: Negative meaning, and ir- before r: irresponsible.

items.en: The staff were friendly and very helpful when we got lost.
items.gap: The staff were friendly and very ____ when we got lost.
items.explanation: -ful = full of help; -less would mean they could not help at all.

items.en: Without a ticket it is impossible to get into the stadium.
items.gap: Without a ticket it is ____ to get into the stadium.
items.explanation: 'Without a ticket' — no way in → negative, and im- before p.

items.en: Her dream is to become a scientist and study the brain.
items.gap: Her dream is to become a ____ and study the brain.
items.explanation: -ist = the person: science → scientist.

items.en: The politician promised lower taxes at every rally.
items.gap: The ____ promised lower taxes at every rally.
items.explanation: -ian = the person: politics → politician.

items.en: My employer lets me work from home two days a week.
items.gap: My ____ lets me work from home two days a week.
items.explanation: -er = the person or company that GIVES the work; -ee = the person who does it.

items.en: In August the old town is completely full of tourists.
items.gap: In August the old town is completely full of ____.
items.explanation: -ist person noun, and the plural: tour → tourists.

items.en: The two countries want to strengthen their trade links.
items.gap: The two countries want to ____ their trade links.
items.explanation: Adjective → verb: strong → strength + -en. After 'want to' you need a verb.

items.en: They decided to shorten the meeting to thirty minutes.
items.gap: They decided to ____ the meeting to thirty minutes.
items.explanation: Adjective → verb with -en: short → shorten.

items.en: She passed the driving test easily at her first attempt.
items.gap: She passed the driving test ____ at her first attempt.
items.explanation: Adverb describing 'passed': easy → easily (y → i).

items.en: Crossing the tracks here is extremely dangerous.
items.gap: Crossing the tracks here is extremely ____.
items.explanation: Noun → adjective with -ous: danger → dangerous.

items.en: I completely forgot about our meeting yesterday.
items.gap: I ____ forgot about our meeting yesterday.
items.explanation: Adverb describing 'forgot': complete → completely.

items.en: Could you speak more slowly, please? I can't follow you.
items.gap: Could you speak more ____, please? I can't follow you.
items.explanation: Adverb describing 'speak': slow → slowly.

items.en: Three musicians were playing jazz in the square.
items.gap: Three ____ were playing jazz in the square.
items.explanation: -ian person noun, and the plural: music → musicians.

items.en: The city plans to widen the road next year.
items.gap: The city plans to ____ the road next year.
items.explanation: Adjective → verb with -en: wide → widen. After 'plans to' you need a verb.
